messages.content: Write a short announcement for a new feature in a note-taking app: offline sync. Around 200 words.

**Notes now work without a connection**

Starting today, the app saves everything you write locally first, then syncs it the moment you're back online. Write on a plane, in a tunnel, or anywhere signal drops, and your notes wait for you exactly as you left them.

Here's how it works: every edit saves to your device immediately. When the app detects a connection, it pushes changes to your other devices and pulls down anything you missed. If you edited the same note on two devices while offline, the app merges the changes automatically and flags any real conflicts for you to review, so you never lose text without knowing.

A few things worth knowing:

- Offline sync applies to all note types, including checklists and attachments under 10MB.
- You can check sync status anytime from the note list — a small icon shows whether a note is saved locally, syncing, or fully up to date.
- Existing notes update to the new sync engine automatically; no action is needed on your part.

We built this after hearing from users who take notes on commutes, in the field, or anywhere connectivity is unreliable. Update the app to get it now.

Questions or issues? Reach out through the in-app feedback form.
Add a paragraph about what happens when two devices edit the same note offline.

Here's the announcement with a new paragraph added on offline conflicts:

**Notes now work without a connection**

Starting today, the app saves everything you write locally first, then syncs it the moment you're back online. Write on a plane, in a tunnel, or anywhere signal drops, and your notes wait for you exactly as you left them.

If you edited the same note on two devices while offline, the app merges the changes automatically and flags any real conflicts for you to review, so you never lose text without knowing.

If you and, say, a shared editor both change the same note while offline, sync reconciles it line by line once you're back online. Non-overlapping edits merge without any input from you — add a line at the top on your phone, add one at the bottom on your laptop, and both show up. Only edits that touch the same line get flagged: the app keeps both versions and drops a conflict marker in the note so you can pick or combine them by hand. Nothing gets overwritten or silently dropped.

A few things worth knowing:

- Offline sync applies to all note types, including checklists and attachments under 10MB.
- You can check sync status anytime from the note list — a small icon shows whether a note is saved locally, syncing, or fully up to date.
- Existing notes update to the new sync engine automatically; no action is needed on your part.

We built this after hearing from users who take notes on commutes, in the field, or anywhere connectivity is unreliable. Update the app to get it now.

Questions or issues? Reach out through the in-app feedback form.
